entry.title: Introducing OpenPedCanExpress
entry.content:
We are excited to share OpenPedCanExpress, a new web tool for exploring gene expression across pediatric tumors and normal tissue controls! Search any gene and instantly compare its expression in pediatric brain tumors against normal brain tissue, all in your browser with no code required.

You can compare primary tumors from PBTA, TARGET, GMKF, and DGD by histology and molecular subtype. Normal controls include GTEx brain, pediatric normal brain regions, developmental timepoints, and brain cell types. Plots are interactive, with per-sample tooltips and a log2 scale toggle. You can also export publication-ready figures as PDF, JPG, PNG, or SVG at 300 DPI.

OpenPedCanExpress is built on data from the OpenPedCan project and uses the same plot groups and color scheme as TAPESTRY for consistency across our tools. Try it at rokitalab.github.io/OpenPedCanExpress, and find the code on GitHub. We would love to hear your feedback!

entry.title: Remembering John Matthew for Childhood Cancer Awareness Month

link.title: Remembering John Matthew for Childhood Cancer Awareness Month

entry.content:
On this last day of Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, I’m remembering my little cousin, John Matthew Dean. John Matthew was born on November 21, 1993, and passed away in August of 1998 after a battle with a malignant brain tumor. He was four years old.

Kids like John Matthew are why our lab exists. Brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer-related death in children, and too many families still face a diagnosis with too few options. Every dataset we analyze and every target we nominate is in service of changing that for the next child.

To every child and family affected by childhood cancer, and to everyone working to end it: we see you, and we’re not stopping. 💛

You can read more about John Matthew on my personal site.

entry.title: Rokita Lab returns to AACR Pediatrics

link.title: Rokita Lab returns to AACR Pediatrics

entry.content:
So proud of Dr. Ryan Corbett and Dr. Meg Goswami, who represented the Rokita Lab at the 2026 American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Pediatric Cancer Conference! 🎉

They presented two posters. The first describes how tumor-specific splicing can nominate new therapeutic targets for pediatric brain tumors. The second introduces our web app, which lets researchers explore this splicing landscape without writing any code. You can try it yourself at tapestry.rokitalab.com.

Thank you to everyone who stopped by for the thoughtful questions and conversations. Thank you also to all of our co-authors, whose work made these posters possible. Here’s to renewed inspiration and new collaborations in the fight against pediatric brain cancer. ✨
entry.summary: So proud of Dr. Ryan Corbett and Dr. Meg Goswami, who represented the Rokita Lab at the 2026 American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Pediatric Cancer Conference! 🎉

entry.title: Dylan Mach joins the Rokita Lab!

link.title: Dylan Mach joins the Rokita Lab!

entry.content:
We are excited to welcome Dylan Mach, a second-year undergraduate student at The George Washington University, to the Rokita Lab 🎉. Dylan is majoring in Biology and minoring in Statistics, and is part of GWU’s Seven-Year BA/MD program.

Dylan is interested in bioinformatics research and previously used hierarchical generalized additive models to explore relationships between urban planning and public health, developing an urban health index from that work. He also brings wet-lab experience in biology and is excited to approach medicine from a dry-lab perspective in the Rokita Lab.

Dylan is passionate about using quantitative methods to tackle challenges in medicine. Outside of the lab, he enjoys playing the violin, reading, and watching baseball games at Nationals Park.

Welcome, Dylan! 👏

entry.title: Our very first Rokita Lab retreat!

link.title: Our very first Rokita Lab retreat!

entry.content:
So grateful for 1.5 days of dedicated Rokita Lab time this week with our amazing scientist team — Dr. Ryan Corbett, Dr. Patricia Sullivan, Dr. Meg Goswami, and Dr. Chao Di.

It was our very first dedicated lab retreat, and we made the most of every minute: diving into our many active projects, planning new experiments, strategizing on current and future grants, and envisioning each manuscript ahead.

I’m walking away energized and thankful for a team that brings so much talent, curiosity, creativity, and heart to our mission of improving outcomes for children with brain tumors. The best ideas happen when we give ourselves the time to think. ✨

entry.title: A great day at the CCIR Retreat

link.title: A great day at the CCIR Retreat

entry.content:
It was great to be back at Children’s National Hospital for the annual Center for Cancer and Immunology Research (CCIR) Retreat!

A real highlight was meeting several Rokita Lab and BTI Bioinformatics Core members in person for the first time. Dr. Corbett and Dr. Goswami both gave flash talks on behalf of the lab and did a fantastic job representing our work — congratulations to Ryan on winning best flash talk of his session! 🏆

The whole day was educational, fun, and a great reminder of just how much science is happening across CCIR. Days like this are also the clearest argument for team science: the questions we care most about in pediatric cancer don’t get answered by any one lab or discipline alone. Excited for what comes next.

Big thanks to the organizers for putting it all together!
entry.summary: It was great to be back at Children’s National Hospital for the annual Center for Cancer and Immunology Research (CCIR) Retreat!

entry.title: BTI Bioinformatics Core dedicates a retreat to engineering and automation

link.title: BTI Bioinformatics Core dedicates a retreat to engineering and automation

entry.content:
While part of the team was on the other side of the world at ISPNO, Bailey, Rehman, Alex, and Aylar spent a day and a half at a focused Bioinformatics Operations retreat, dedicated entirely to engineering and automation.

The goal: design a data model to support archiving Cavatica workflow versions, and build a framework for associating those workflow versions with their corresponding files hosted on S3. The retreat combined collaborative planning, data model design, and hands-on development to push forward the Core’s data warehousing and research operations capabilities.

Thank you, Bailey, Rehman, Alex, and Aylar, for carving out this time to build infrastructure that will pay off for the whole Core.

entry.title: Rokita Lab science on display at ISPNO in Sydney

link.title: Rokita Lab science on display at ISPNO in Sydney

entry.content:
The Rokita Lab traveled to Sydney this week for the International Symposium on Pediatric Neuro-Oncology (ISPNO), where we shared our latest work with the global pediatric neuro-oncology community.

We shared new work on tumor-enriched splicing across the Pediatric Brain Tumor Atlas (PBTA), and introduced TAPESTRY, our new tool for interactive splicing visualization. Ryan Corbett presented a poster on our compendium of tumor-enriched splice junctions in the PBTA, and Dr. Patricia Sullivan presented a poster on using TAPESTRY to interactively explore tumor-specific alternative splicing in pediatric CNS tumors. Patricia also demoed TAPESTRY live at the Children’s Brain Tumor Network Lunchtime Symposium.

Ryan and Patricia were fantastic ambassadors for the lab, and we’re grateful for every conversation they had with the community in Sydney. Excited to keep sharing our work and TAPESTRY as it grows!
